parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آقشام (akşam), from earlier آخشام (ahşam), from Sogdian 𐫟𐫢𐫀𐫖 (xšʾm /⁠xšām⁠/, “evening”).
From Ottoman Turkish بورج (borc), ultimately from Sogdian 𐼾𐼴𐽀𐼿 (pwrč).

From Ottoman Turkish كنت (kent, “village, town, city”), from older كند (kend), from Sogdian 𐼸𐼻𐼹𐼳 (knδh /⁠kand⁠/, “city”). Compare Old Uyghur 𐽷𐽺𐽸 (knd /⁠kend⁠/, “city, settlement”). Possibly cognate with Northern Kurdish gund (“village”). Most likely not related to Finnish kenttä (“field”).

parole.significato: fasting, abstinence or mortification for religious reasons, especially abstinence from food
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوروج (oruc), from Sogdian [script needed] (rōçag), shares common origins with Persian روزه (ruze, “fasting”).

parole.significato: sparrow, any small perching bird in the family Passeridae, especially the house sparrow
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سرچه (serçe), from Early Old Oghuz سجا (seçē), ultimately from Sogdian 𐼼𐼷𐼿𐼷 (sycy). Cognates Cognate with Azerbaijani sərçə, Chuvash ҫерҫи (śerś̬i), Early Old Oghuz سَجا (seçe), Salar sece and Turkmen serçe.
